newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Chamber sees expansion continuing next year.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Chamber sees expansion continuing next year.

text.p: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce Thursday said it expected the economy to continue expanding next year with inflation remaining under control.

"We continue to expect the economy in 1997 to grow at close to its long-term trend, with modest job growth, low unemployment, stable inflation and interest rates steady or even down a bit," chief economist Martin Regalia said.
The business group predicted the economy would grow by 2.3 percent in 1997 after an estimated 2.4 percent increase in the current year.
It estimated that the Consumer Price Index would rise 2.9 percent next year, identical with the increase anticipated by the business group for this year.
Unemployment, estimated at a 5.4 percent for this year, is expected to turn up slightly to 5.6 percent in 1997.
Interest rates, as measured by the 30-year treasury bond, are predicted to drift downward to 6.5 percent from 6.7 percent in the forecast for this year.
